title: Payment system requirements
idea: Scoping a payment system means naming who pays, who refunds and who confirms, the one money guarantee that matters most, and what v1 leaves out.
points: Customers pay an order by UPI or card and can check its status.
Merchants issue full or partial refunds, never more than was paid.
The core rule: one Idempotency-Key never charges the customer twice.
Assume slow, unreliable gateways; a timeout means unknown, not failed.

hero.title: Actors and use cases in v1

edges.caption: The customer pays one order. Each request carries an Idempotency-Key, so a retry never charges twice.
The customer then sees SUCCEEDED, FAILED, or PROCESSING while the result is still unknown.

edges.label: confirms
edges.caption: UPI often finishes later. The gateway is an actor: it reports the final result by webhook.
A merchant refunds part or all of a successful payment, one refund at a time.

edges.label: settles
edges.caption: A system job asks the gateway about payments stuck in PROCESSING and records the answer.
Saved cards, split payouts and multi-currency wait for later. Naming them early keeps the interview focused.

code.title: Use cases as an enum
code.caption: The scope as code: each use case has one actor, and v1 is an explicit set.

walk.text: v1 is a named EnumSet. Anything missing from it is out of scope.
Print every use case with an IN or OUT tag and its actor.
Four actors: customer, merchant, the gateway itself, and a system job.
Seven v1 use cases: pay by UPI, pay by card, check, retry, refund, confirm, reconcile.
Saved cards, split payouts and multi-currency are listed, so the cut is visible.

pitfalls: Do not treat a gateway timeout as a failure; the money may have moved.
State volume and latency targets as assumptions, never as measured facts.
Name the out-of-scope list aloud so the interviewer can redirect early.

quiz.q: A UPI charge times out at the gateway. Which v1 rule fits?
options: Mark it FAILED and let the customer pay again
Keep it PROCESSING until the webhook or reconciler decides
Charge again at once with a new Idempotency-Key
Refund it immediately to be safe
quiz.why: A timeout says nothing about the money. FAILED invites a second charge; PROCESSING waits for the gateway's real answer.

takeaway: Agree on actors, use cases and the charge-once rule before any class.

starters: Why is the payment gateway treated as an actor?
Should saved cards ever be in v1 scope?
Which scale assumptions should I state for a payment system?
